ABX.title: Compounded Medications for Infections and Parasites
ABX.intro: Antibiotics, antifungals, antivirals and antiparasitic medications are often hard to give in the strength or form a patient needs, especially to children, cats and small dogs. We compound these ingredients into flavored liquids, treats, capsules, creams and ear packs so they are easier to give. Your prescriber or veterinarian chooses the medication, strength and length of treatment.

SKIN.title: Compounded Skin and Hair Medications
SKIN.intro: Dermatology compounding lets a prescriber combine ingredients, adjust strengths and choose a base that suits the skin, such as a cream, gel, serum, foam or ointment. We prepare compounded topicals for acne, melasma and dark spots, hair thinning, rosacea, fungal infections, scars and itchy or inflamed skin, for people and pets.

GI.title: Compounded Stomach and Digestion Medications
GI.intro: Medicines for nausea, reflux, slow stomach emptying, constipation and diarrhea are often needed in small or unusual strengths, or in a form that is easy to swallow. We compound these ingredients as flavored suspensions, capsules, suppositories and transdermal gels for people and pets.

NUTR.title: Compounded Vitamins and Nutrients
NUTR.intro: Some patients need a vitamin or nutrient in a specific strength, without dyes or fillers, or in a form a child or pet will take. We compound vitamins, minerals and other nutrients from prescriptions, in capsules, flavored liquids and chewable treats.

BEHAV.title: Compounded Medications for Behavior, Mood and Sleep
BEHAV.intro: Mood, anxiety, sleep and behavior medications are prescribed for people and, often off-label, for pets with anxiety or compulsive behaviors. Compounding allows small strengths for cats and small dogs, flavored liquids and treats, and transdermal gels for pets who refuse pills.

HEART.title: Compounded Heart and Blood Pressure Medications
HEART.intro: Heart and blood pressure medicines frequently need precise, small strengths, especially for cats and dogs with heart disease. We compound these ingredients in flavored liquids, treats, capsules and transdermal gels, and in strengths that commercial tablets don't come in, from your prescriber's or veterinarian's order.

PAIN.title: Compounded Pain and Inflammation Medications
PAIN.intro: Compounded pain medications include topical creams that combine several ingredients, low-dose naltrexone (LDN), and anti-inflammatory medicines in forms that are easier to take. Topicals can be applied to the area that hurts. Your prescriber decides which ingredients and strengths are right for you.

URO.title: Compounded Kidney and Urinary Medications
URO.intro: Kidney and bladder medications for people and pets are often needed in small strengths or in forms that are easier to give every day, such as flavored liquids and treats. We compound medicines for urinary incontinence, bladder spasms, phosphate control in kidney disease and related conditions.

ALLERGY.title: Compounded Allergy and Breathing Medications
ALLERGY.intro: Allergy and breathing medications can be compounded without dyes, fillers or common allergens, in custom strengths and in forms such as flavored liquids, capsules, nasal sprays and transdermal gels. This is an option for people with mast cell activation syndrome or sensitivities, and for pets who won't take tablets.

MEN.title: Compounded Men's and Sexual Health Medications
MEN.intro: Men's health compounding includes testosterone and other hormone preparations, hair-loss topicals, and medications prescribed for sexual health, in creams, capsules, troches and rapid-dissolve tablets. Your prescriber orders the ingredients and strengths and monitors your treatment.

IMMUNE.title: Compounded Immune and Cancer Care Medications
IMMUNE.intro: Immune-modulating and cancer-care medications are prescribed for people and pets in strengths and forms that often aren't sold commercially, such as small-strength capsules and flavored liquids for cats and dogs. Some of these are hazardous drugs, which we handle following USP <800> safe-handling standards.

ENDO.title: Compounded Endocrine and Metabolic Medications
ENDO.intro: Endocrine and metabolic conditions, such as adrenal disorders and diabetes-related problems in people and pets, often call for doses that need to be precise and adjusted over time. We compound these medicines in capsules, flavored liquids and other forms from your prescriber's or veterinarian's order.

NEURO.title: Compounded Medications for Seizures and Nerve Pain
NEURO.intro: Seizure and nerve pain medications need consistent, accurate dosing. Compounding allows strengths between commercial tablet sizes, flavored liquids for children and pets, and topical creams for nerve pain. Your prescriber or veterinarian sets the dose and any blood level monitoring.

HRT.title: Compounded Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT)
HRT.intro: Compounded hormone therapy lets your prescriber choose the hormones, strengths and form, such as a cream, troche, capsule or vaginal preparation. We prepare estradiol, estriol, progesterone, testosterone, DHEA and combinations like Biest. Compounded hormones are not FDA-approved, and your prescriber monitors your treatment.

NUMB.title: Compounded Numbing Creams and Topical Anesthetics
NUMB.intro: Topical anesthetics are compounded for procedures such as cosmetic injections, laser treatments and tattooing, and for other uses your prescriber directs. Combination creams such as BLT combine benzocaine, lidocaine and tetracaine in one preparation. Use only the amount directed, on the area directed.

LIVER.title: Compounded Liver Support Medications
LIVER.intro: Liver support medications are prescribed for people and, frequently, for dogs and cats with liver disease. Compounding gives veterinarians small strengths and flavored or treat forms that make daily dosing easier.

THY.title: Compounded Thyroid Medications
THY.intro: Thyroid compounding includes T4 and T3 in custom strengths and combinations, and slow-release capsules, for people, and methimazole in transdermal gel, flavored liquid or treat form for cats with hyperthyroidism. Your prescriber or veterinarian monitors thyroid levels and adjusts the dose.

EENT.title: Compounded Eye, Ear and Nose Medications
EENT.intro: Compounded nasal sprays, ear preparations and related medications let a prescriber combine ingredients or choose a strength that isn't sold commercially. We prepare nonsterile nasal sprays and ear preparations for people and pets from a prescription.

ORAL.title: Compounded Mouth and Throat Medications
ORAL.intro: Mouth and throat preparations such as compounded mouthwashes and lollipops are used for mouth sores, dry mouth and soreness, including sores caused by cancer treatment. Your prescriber chooses the ingredients and how often to use them.

__combo.name: Combination preparations
__combo.title: Compounded Combination Preparations
__combo.intro: Some patients need several ingredients that aren't sold together. Compounding lets us put them into one preparation, in the strengths and ratio your prescriber orders, such as a pain cream, a hormone cream or a nasal spray. That can mean fewer separate medications to take or apply.

Capsule.title: Compounded Capsules
Capsule.intro: Compounded capsules are made in the exact strength a prescriber orders, including strengths between or below commercial tablet sizes. We can leave out dyes, lactose and other fillers when needed, and combine more than one ingredient in a single capsule. For pets, capsules can often be hidden in a treat.

Flavored oral suspension.title: Compounded Flavored Liquids (Oral Suspensions)
Flavored oral suspension.intro: A flavored suspension turns a tablet into a liquid that is measured with an oral syringe, so small or changing doses are easy to give. Flavors such as chicken, tuna, beef and bacon help pets take it, and fruit or bubblegum flavors help children. Shake well before each dose and check the label for storage.

Cream.title: Compounded Creams
Cream.intro: Compounded creams can combine several ingredients and deliver them to the area of skin your prescriber directs. They are used for pain, hormone therapy, skin conditions and numbing. Metered dispensers such as Topi-CLICK help you apply the same amount each time.

Oral liquid.title: Compounded Oral Liquids
Oral liquid.intro: Oral liquids are an option for people and pets who can't swallow tablets or capsules, or who need a dose that's easy to adjust. Each dose is measured with the oral syringe we provide. Some liquids are refrigerated, so check your label.

Transdermal gel (PLO).title: Compounded Transdermal Gels for Pets (PLO)
Transdermal gel (PLO).intro: Transdermal gels are rubbed onto the hairless inner ear, which is useful for cats and dogs who won't take pills. They come in pre-measured syringes. Wear a glove when applying and alternate ears if your veterinarian directs. Not every medication is absorbed well through the skin, so your veterinarian decides when this form is a good fit.

Chewable treat.title: Compounded Chewable Treats for Pets
Chewable treat.intro: Medicated chewable treats are flavored so dogs and cats take them like a snack, which can make daily medications easier to give. Each treat contains the strength your veterinarian orders. Keep treats sealed, out of reach of pets, and stored as the label directs.

Tablet.title: Compounded Tablets
Tablet.intro: Compounded tablets are prepared in strengths that aren't available commercially, such as low-dose naltrexone. Take them by mouth exactly as directed on your label.

Vaginal preparation.title: Compounded Vaginal Preparations
Vaginal preparation.intro: Compounded vaginal preparations include creams and inserts made with hormones or other ingredients your prescriber orders. They are inserted with an applicator or dispenser, usually at bedtime.

Ear pack.title: Compounded Ear Packs for Pets
Ear pack.intro: Ear packs are a long-acting gel placed in a pet's ear canal, often by the veterinarian, that stays in place for several days. They can combine an antibiotic, antifungal and anti-inflammatory ingredient in one treatment, which means fewer daily ear treatments at home.

Ointment.title: Compounded Ointments
Ointment.intro: Ointments are thicker than creams and hold ingredients on the skin longer, which is why they are often chosen for dry or cracked areas and some rectal and anal preparations. Apply a thin layer to the area directed.

Suppository.title: Compounded Suppositories
Suppository.intro: Suppositories are useful when a medication can't be swallowed, such as during nausea and vomiting, or when it is meant to act locally. We compound them in the strength your prescriber orders. Many are kept cool or refrigerated.

Slow-release capsule.title: Compounded Slow-Release Capsules
Slow-release capsule.intro: Slow-release capsules release the medication gradually over several hours. They are commonly used for T3 thyroid medication. Swallow them whole: do not open, crush or chew them.

Troche.title: Compounded Troches
Troche.intro: A troche is a small, flavored lozenge that dissolves slowly between the cheek and gum, so some of the medication is absorbed through the lining of the mouth. Troches are often used for hormone therapy. Avoid eating or drinking until it has fully dissolved.

Gel.title: Compounded Gels
Gel.intro: Compounded gels dry quickly and are not greasy, which suits the face, scalp and areas where a cream would feel heavy. They are applied to the area directed and allowed to dry.

Nasal spray.title: Compounded Nasal Sprays
Nasal spray.intro: Compounded nasal sprays can combine ingredients that aren't sold together, such as the BEG spray used for sinus symptoms, or deliver a medication your prescriber wants in the nose. Prime the pump before first use.

Powder.title: Compounded Powders
Powder.intro: Compounded powders are measured and mixed with food or a liquid, or used on the skin, as your label directs. They are handy when a large or flexible dose is needed.

Serum.title: Compounded Serums
Serum.intro: Compounded serums are light, fast-absorbing preparations for the skin and scalp, often used for hair thinning and pigment concerns. Apply to clean, dry skin or scalp as directed.

Rapid-dissolve tablet.title: Compounded Rapid-Dissolve Tablets
Rapid-dissolve tablet.intro: Rapid-dissolve tablets melt under the tongue in seconds, with no water needed. They suit people who have trouble swallowing pills. Avoid eating or drinking until the tablet has fully dissolved.

Mouthwash.title: Compounded Mouthwashes
Mouthwash.intro: Compounded mouthwashes, sometimes called magic mouthwash, combine ingredients such as a numbing agent, an antihistamine and a coating agent for mouth sores and soreness. Swish and spit or swallow exactly as directed.

Solution.title: Compounded Solutions
Solution.intro: Compounded solutions are clear liquids for use on the skin, in the mouth or by mouth, depending on the medication. Use them exactly as the label directs.

pets.title: Compounded Medications for Pets
pets.intro: Most medications are made for people, in strengths and forms that don't suit a 10-pound cat or a 100-pound dog. We compound for dogs, cats and exotic pets in flavored liquids, chewable treats, transdermal ear gels, ear packs and small-strength capsules, from your veterinarian's prescription. Pharmacy on the Park holds Pharmacon veterinary compounding certification.

people.title: Compounded Medications for People
people.intro: Compounding lets your prescriber order a medication in a strength, form or flavor that isn't sold commercially, or without dyes, fillers or allergens. We prepare creams, capsules, troches, rapid-dissolve tablets, nasal sprays and more for adults and children, from a prescription.
